75-023.r: Refineries: Barauni → Bihar; Bongaigaon → Assam; Bina → Madhya Pradesh; Koyali → Gujarat.

75-025.r: Map question: area 3 = Cauvery onshore basin, Tamil Nadu, where commercial production of mineral oil started recently.

75-026.r: Mangala, Bhagyam, Shakti, Aishwarya → oil fields found in the Barmer-Sanchore basin; Mangala is India's largest onshore hydrocarbon field.

75-027.r: 14 NELP blocks, 1 JV block, 2 nomination blocks and 4 CBM blocks → petroleum exploration.

75-028.r: 'Hydrogen Vision-2025' → linked by the book to warehousing (storage) of petroleum products.
75-028.c: The document meant is usually called 'Hydrocarbon Vision 2025', a long-term plan for the whole petroleum (hydrocarbon) sector.

75-029.r: Strategic crude oil reserves (ISPRL) → Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru, Padur; Ankleshwar was not selected.

75-030.r: Oil exploration in India → Oil India Ltd. (among the options); ONGC is the other key explorer.

75-031.r: HBJ pipeline → carries natural gas from the South Basin, offshore near Bombay High.

75-032.r: Hazira-Bijapur-Jagdishpur (HBJ) gas pipeline → built by Gas Authority of India Limited (GAIL).

75-033.r: HVJ gas pipeline has pumping stations at all four: Aonla, Auraiya, Babrala, Guna → the book gives no single answer (*).

75-034.r: Reliance's big gas find → coastal Andhra: D-6 block of the Krishna-Godavari (KG) basin, India's biggest gas reserve (2002-03); KG basin spreads over 50,000 sq km.

75-036.r: Most natural gas → western offshore, mainly Bombay High. 2024-25 (P): 36.11 BCM; offshore 71.81%, Assam 9.83%, Rajasthan 4.95%.

75-037.r: Wrong statement: Bombay High lies 160 km (not 60 km) off Mumbai. It was found by a Russian–Indian team and is run by ONGC.

75-038.r: Shale gas priority basins in India: Cambay, Krishna-Godavari, Cauvery and Damodar Valley → all three (1, 2 and 3).

75-039.r: Wood → biofuel, not a fossil fuel. Fossil fuels (from buried plants and animals): coal, petroleum, diesel, kerosene, natural gas.

75-040.r: Pipeline lengths: HBJ gas 6718 km > Salaya-Koyali-Mathura 2663 > Jamnagar-Loni LPG 1427 > Kandla-Bhatinda 1413 → order 2>1>3>4, no option; CGPSC's (c) is wrong per the book.

76-001.r: Major minerals: chromite, kyanite, sillimanite. Bentonite → minor mineral (like fuller's earth, granite, gypsum, dolomite, marble) → 2, 3 and 4.

76-002.r: Odisha → monopoly in chromite output; largest manganese and bauxite reserves (1 April 2020). Top silver producer → Rajasthan. Statements (a) and (d) both true: no single answer (*).

76-003.r: Wrong: Copper–Chitradurga (Chitradurga has iron ore, manganese) and Manganese–Bhilwara (Bhilwara: copper). Correct: Iron ore–Ballari (Karnataka), Bauxite–Katni (Madhya Pradesh).

76-004.r: Asbestos: only producer Andhra Pradesh (2013-14); largest reserve Rajasthan (1 April 2020). Question asks production, so no option fits; the book gives no single answer (*).

76-005.r: Only 2 true: Kodarma (Jharkhand) → mica, 'Mica City of India'. Oil and gas → Tertiary sedimentary rocks; old Gondwana and Dharwar rocks are poor in them.

76-006.r: Kodarma (Jharkhand) → world-famous for mica, especially ruby mica. Natural gas → sedimentary (marine) basins, not Dharwar; petroleum → KG, Cauvery, Assam, Gujarat, Rajasthan, not Aravallis.
76-006.c: BPSC's key also takes only (b): diamonds are classically linked with the Vindhyan system (Panna, Golconda), so 'Cuddapah series is famous for diamonds' counts as false, though the book lists diamond among Cuddapah basin minerals.

76-007.r: Garnet → metamorphic mineral, formed only at the high temperature and pressure of metamorphism.

76-008.r: Quartzite → non-foliated metamorphic rock, almost all quartz; forms from quartz-rich sandstone.

76-009.r: Manganese → Madhya Pradesh; Nickel → Odisha; Lead-zinc → Rajasthan; Asbestos → Andhra Pradesh.

76-010.r: Largest manganese ore producer → Madhya Pradesh (2023-24, P; IMYB 2024).

76-011.r: Manganese 2013-14: Madhya Pradesh > Odisha > Andhra Pradesh > Rajasthan. 2023-24 (P): Madhya Pradesh > Maharashtra > Odisha > Karnataka > Andhra Pradesh.

76-012.r: Top producers (IMYB 2022): iron ore → Odisha; copper ore → Madhya Pradesh; gold ore → Karnataka; mica → Rajasthan. No code fits; the book gives no single answer (*).

76-013.r: India is self-sufficient in none of tin, silver, gold, graphite. World graphite reserves 280 million t: China 28%, Brazil 26%, India only 3%. No single answer (*).

76-014.r: Top producers: Mineral oil (crude) → Gujarat (2024-25); Gypsum → Rajasthan; Gold → Karnataka; Bauxite → Odisha.
76-014.c: The book prints * (no single answer), but its own match (Gujarat, Rajasthan, Karnataka, Odisha) is code 3 4 2 1, which is option (d).

76-015.r: Rajasthan → known for deposits of limestone, gypsum, salt and zinc.

76-016.r: Gypsum → non-metallic mineral (with phosphorite, dolomite, garnet, bentonite, asbestos, feldspar, kaolin, sillimanite, limestone). Haematite, bauxite, limonite are metallic ores.
76-016.c: The book's list of non-metallic minerals also names cadmium, vanadium and gallium, which are metals.

76-018.r: Gypsum → abundant in the Churu-Bikaner-Sri Ganganagar belt; a pollution source, raises soil fertility, and after value addition is used in health and building.

76-019.r: Coal → Karanpura (Jharkhand); Gold → Hutti (Karnataka); Mica → Nellore (Andhra Pradesh); Manganese → Bhandara (Maharashtra).

76-020.r: Makum → coal; Dalli Rajhara → iron ore; Koraput → bauxite; Chitradurga → manganese.

76-021.r: Wrong pair: Kamptee–Copper; Kamptee (Maharashtra) → coal. Correct: Amguri (Assam)–petroleum, Lanjigarh (Odisha)–bauxite, Bellary (Karnataka)–iron ore.

76-022.r: Badam Pahar (Odisha) → iron ore; Kodarma (Jharkhand) → mica; Mosabani (Jharkhand) → copper; Rava (Krishna-Godavari basin) → petroleum.

76-023.r: Iron-ore zones: Badam Pahar → Odisha; Dalli-Rajhara → Chhattisgarh; Kudremukh → Karnataka; Noamundi → Jharkhand.

76-024.r: Wrong pair: Nellore–Manganese; Nellore (Andhra Pradesh) → mica and copper. Correct: Dalli-Rajhara–iron ore, Rakha–copper, Amarkantak–bauxite.

76-025.r: Graphite → Rampa (Andhra Pradesh); Lead → Zawar (Rajasthan); Salt → Didwana (Rajasthan); Silver → Bellary (Karnataka).

76-026.r: Ankleshwar (Bharuch, Gujarat) → petroleum; Dalli Rajhara → iron ore (captive mines of Bhilai Steel Plant); Kodarma → mica; Khetri → copper.

76-027.r: Iron ore → Keonjhar; Copper → Khetri; Coal → Korba; Mica → Kodarma.

76-028.r: Copper–Gold–Iron–Coal = Khetri (Rajasthan) – Kolar (Karnataka) – Kudremukh – Jharia (Dhanbad, coking coal).
76-028.h: Three K's then a J: Khetri, Kolar, Kudremukh, Jharia = Copper, Gold, Iron, Coal.

76-030.r: Chromite → Odisha produces almost the entire output (2023-24, P; IMYB 2024): a near monopoly.

76-031.r: Gypsum → Jamsar; Copper → Khoh-Dariba; Rock phosphate → Jhamar-kotra; Lead & Zinc → Rampura-Agucha.

76-032.r: Khetri (Jhunjhunu, Rajasthan) → copper; Jharia (Jharkhand) → coal for coke; Singhbhum (Jharkhand) → iron ore.

76-033.r: Wrong pair: Bailadila–Madhya Pradesh; Bailadila is in Chhattisgarh. Correct: Kemmangundi–Karnataka, Singhbhum–Jharkhand, Mayurbhanj–Odisha.

76-034.r: Diamond → Panna; Iron ore → Bastar, Durg; Bauxite → Surguja, Mandla, Satna, Balaghat, Bilaspur; Coal → Sidhi, Shahdol, Chhindwara, Betul, Raigarh.

76-035.r: Coal → Talcher (Angul, Odisha, on the Brahmani); Copper → Khetri (Jhunjhunu); Iron ore → Kudremukh (Chikmagalur); Silver → Zawar (Udaipur).

76-036.r: Wrong pair: Manganese–Koraput; Koraput is famous for aluminium (bauxite). Correct: Iron ore–Kudremukh, Copper–Khetri, Coal–Singareni.

76-037.r: Copper → Khetri; Gas plant → Auraiya; Aluminium → Korba; Petroleum (refinery) → Kochi.

76-038.r: Neither true: Balaghat → manganese (with Jabalpur, Jhabua, Chhindwara); Majhgawan (Panna, MP) → diamonds, about one million carats.

76-039.r: Granite slabs and slates → Lalitpur (UP). Granite in Uttar Pradesh: Lalitpur, Mahoba, Banda.

76-040.r: Diamond mines → Madhya Pradesh: Panna (biggest diamond-mining centre) and Satna districts.

76-041.r: Diamond-bearing kimberlite → Raipur area: Payalikhand and Behradin (now Gariaband district), plus Tokapal (Bastar), Chhattisgarh.

76-042.r: Sonbhadra (UP) → andalusite, pyrite, dolomite (also fireclay, limestone, china clay, potash). Uranium is found in Lalitpur, not Sonbhadra.

76-043.r: Kerala beach sands → ilmenite, zircon, sillimanite (also rutile, leucoxene, monazite); not tungsten. World-class deposit between Neendakara and Kayamkulam.

76-044.r: Ilmenite and rutile → main sources of titanium. Heavy mineral sands: rutile, zircon, sillimanite, garnet, ilmenite, monazite, leucoxene.
